lesson: Situation: orchestrator presented a design.md link to the user alongside its own bulleted summary that restated and interpreted the design's analytical content (cohort structure, methods, findings, limitations). Lesson: presenting a design/report link is not the place for the orchestrator's own analytical interpretation of its content — that is study_designer_agent's/peer_reviewer_agent's job. Hand off the link with minimal framing (what it is, that it's ready for review) and let the document speak for itself.

Situation: single-panel plots (forest plot, bar chart, synthesis scatter, steps diagram) were generated at 8x5-13x7 inches with no data-volume justification, causing oversized figures in the rendered report. Lesson: default single-panel plot figsize to no more than 4x4 inches; only exceed that when there is a genuinely large volume of data to show (e.g. a heatmap with many rows/columns, a forest plot with many categories needing height to avoid label overlap) — and even then, only grow the dimension the data volume actually demands (e.g. height, not width).

Situation: design/execution of a GRN immune-age clock (predict_immune_age_grn_clock) step omitted a pre-run feature-coverage check. Lesson: before running any pre-trained expression-based clock/model on a pseudobulk dataset, check gene overlap between the data and the model's required feature genes; hard-fail (skip that run, report the coverage figure) if >20% of required genes are missing rather than running with reduced/degraded coverage silently.

Situation: bullet lists under a label like 'ISSUES:' rendered as one jammed paragraph in the review-artifact HTML. Lesson: python-markdown needs a blank line before a list to recognize it; the renderer (knowhow/render_review_artifact.py) now auto-inserts one, but writers should still put a blank line before any '- ' list for clarity.

Situation: design.md's Data Inventory section asserted the per-lineage *_rna.rds files were raw counts; they were actually log1p-normalized, discovered only when data_analyst_agent loaded them during execution. Lesson: deciding raw-vs-normalized (or any matrix-content-level fact) is not the planner's job — the planner should inspect only metadata (file locations, structure, columns, cell/sample counts, exclusions) during design and never load the actual count/expression matrices; the analyst confirms and handles data representation at execution time.
